title: Ivo and the Cover
premise: Yara Sandoval, a crash investigator haunted by the row-twelve deaths of his family, is handed an impossible case: a passenger flight whose records vanish mid-flight, as if it never existed. The trail leads to Ilse Brandt, a financial defector hiding aboard the plane who carries proof that a Frankfurt trading syndicate engineered the erasure to mask a market manipulation timed for opening bell. As Yara extracts her across three countries while his own agency disowns him, he discovers the syndicate's inside man is his mentor — and that the flight was bait to flush out anyone loyal enough to dig. In the end Yara chooses truth over duty, exposing the cover at Frankfurt's opening bell at the cost of his career, and finds in Ilse and her estranged daughter the beginnings of a family he thought he'd lost forever.
about_author: Xanthe Montrose is the pen name of a former aviation-adjacent journalist who spent years covering regulatory failures before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Yara Sandoval closes another unattributed crash file, unable to sleep after visiting the memorial wall where his family's names sit under row twelve. His colleague Dana urges him to take leave. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief worn down into routine, a man functioning but not living.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dispatch flags an anomaly: flight 4472 is still airborne, yet every booking, manifest, and radar record has been wiped. Yara is pulled in because he once flagged the airline's data contractor. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: professional curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Ghost on the Scope
chapters.summary: Air traffic controller Mirek watches the blip flicker and stabilize, then receives an order to log it as equipment error. He screenshots everything anyway. POV: Mirek. Emotional beat: quiet defiance of a small man deciding to matter.

chapters.title: Manifest of One
chapters.summary: Yara reconstructs a partial manifest from boarding-gate caches: 214 passengers, plus one name that appears in no database — I. Brandt. His mentor, Director Halvorsen, tells him to drop it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the first hook of obsession; duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carried
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt, disguised as a consultant, reviews the encrypted drive in her seatback pocket: evidence tying the Meridian Syndicate to a coordinated erasure timed before Frankfurt open. She knows she's the lure. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: cold fear braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: The plane makes an unscheduled stop in Rijeka under 'maintenance.' Armed men board posing as inspectors. Yara, tracking from Lisbon, realizes someone inside his agency is steering the case away. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sting.

chapters.title: The Contractor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dana helps Yara trace the data-wipe to Helix Systems, whose parent company feeds Meridian's trading algorithms. They find a payment routed through a shell tied to Halvorsen's brother-in-law. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: loyalty tested — she chooses Yara over the institution.

chapters.title: Terminal Night
chapters.summary: Ilse slips the fake inspectors by triggering a fire alarm, vanishing into Rijeka's rain-slicked streets with a burner phone and a dead drop address. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: survival instinct overriding guilt over the passengers she endangered.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One Cab
chapters.summary: Yara reaches Rijeka ahead of the syndicate's cleaners and finds Ilse waiting at the dead drop. Neither trusts the other; both need each other. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two lonely people recognizing damage.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: On a night train to Ljubljana, Ilse confesses the flight may have been staged to draw out anyone who'd notice the erasure — meaning Yara was expected. He refuses to turn back. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love against duty begins its slow ignition.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Hand
chapters.summary: Halvorsen suspends Yara officially, then privately warns him off, revealing he knows about Ilse. Yara records the conversation. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the father-figure revealed as the syndicate's gatekeeper.

chapters.title: Daughter in Vienna
chapters.summary: Ilse's estranged daughter Katrin works at a Vienna bank Meridian uses. Ilse must decide whether using Katrin as an access point makes her protector or predator. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: maternal longing colliding with ruthlessness.

chapters.title: The Cleaners Arrive
chapters.summary: Meridian's fixers hit the safehouse in Ljubljana. Mirek, having leaked radar data to Yara, is caught in the sweep and barely escapes with his screenshots. POV: Mirek. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into commitment.

chapters.title: Encrypted Hearts
chapters.summary: Holed up in Katrin's apartment, Yara decrypts part of Ilse's drive: the erasure masked a short position against the airline itself — they profited from a crash that hadn't happened yet. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Meridian's emissary offers Yara reinstatement, a medal, and his family's case files closed 'honorably' if he surrenders Ilse. He asks for one night to decide. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the abyss of temptation; grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Revisited
chapters.summary: Yara rereads his family's crash report and finds the same Helix fingerprint in its data chain — his family died inside an earlier version of the same cover-up. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: devastation becoming clarity; the personal and professional cases merge.

chapters.title: Katrin's Choice
chapters.summary: Katrin discovers her mother alive and complicit in using her. After a furious confrontation, she hands over her bank credentials anyway — not for Ilse, but because the numbers disgust her. POV: Katrin. Emotional beat: found family forged through anger, not forgiveness.

chapters.title: Night Before the Bell
chapters.summary: The team plans simultaneous disclosure: Mirek's radar logs, Dana's ledger, Katrin's transaction records, all wired to regulators and press, timed to Frankfurt's opening. Halvorsen's counter-move looms. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: taut camaraderie on the eve of war.

chapters.title: Extraction at Dawn
chapters.summary: Meridian takes Ilse at a handoff point; Yara trades himself to get her back, walking into Halvorsen's office carrying the drive as a decoy while Dana executes the release. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the truest form of loyalty.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: At 9:00 a.m. Frankfurt time, the documents go live worldwide. Meridian's position collapses; Halvorsen is arrested mid-briefing; the flight 4472 passengers are confirmed alive, the 'crash' never real. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth landing like a hammer blow.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: A tribunal offers Yara his career back if he softens the record. He declines, instead filing the first honest account of his family's crash, finally giving row twelve its names and cause. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: mourning completed at last.

chapters.title: The Cover We Keep
chapters.summary: Months later, Yara, Ilse, Katrin, Dana, and Mirek share a slow dinner in Rijeka — not heroes, just survivors. Ilse asks what he'll do now; he says, 'Whatever needs attributing.' POV: Yara. Emotional beat: quiet hope; a found family settling into place.
